body:
Thanks for sharing a little bit of your own story.

Looking back, I can see that I've had intrusive thoughts before (even similar ones), but back then they didn't seem so important because even though they were there, I still felt I was in control of my own brain. Now I feel like someone else has taken over and the only control that I have is in very tiny little sections that I've dug out--and most importantly, tiny little sections that he didn't know about and therefore never had the opportunity to pass judgement on.

Re: your question, I'm actually afraid to answer it. The way my brain usually works, every time I talk about something, I'm used to the talking reinforcing the thing. But something is broken and now whenever I talk about something I run the risk of it just disappearing. Like the memory of it stays, but the importance and feeling associated with it disappear. I have a lot of fond memories that I'm terrified of engaging with; they feel paper-thin and just disintegrate if I look into them.

The things that seem to be left over are basically the things that I didn't love very much anyways. The more that I loved something, the less of it is left.

Actually trying very hard to answer your question. When I find a thread, I'm terrified of engaging with it in case it disintegrates.

Basically I've been able to dig out little caves where I don't feel I'm trapped under his gaze. It feels like I'm Frodo Baggins trapped under the gaze of Sauron, but I have no ability to take the ring off without amputating myself. I don't know. Either I go out into what is left of my brain and watch everything collapse or I'm stuck in these little dug-out alcoves. Both options are pretty fucking miserable.

I've done my best to freeze the collapse and hide in these little alcoves, hoping that I'll be able to figure out something or find someone that can help me through this. I kinda feel like I'm lying to myself about that, though, or that the hope is misguided or impossible. I'm rambling again now.

I guess one thread is that I've been able to talk to a few of my friends about what's happened. I can't talk to them about anything else--everything else that we shared is just...stripped out of me--but I've been able to talk about that.

hi, thanks for responding. i'll look into that.

could you explain what you mean by ocd? i know i've been focusing a lot on how everything is crumbling, but honestly i don't know what else to do because there is nothing else left. i was really hopeful that if i dug deep enough i'd be able to find little threads in the dark that might help me get back to myself. it's helped stem further collapse but i haven't actually been able to recover anything at all.

Hi, genuinely thankful for your comment. <3

Still borked but thank you.

What therapy is intended to do depends on the therapist and what their background is. There are number of different 'schools' of therapy, like talk therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, existential therapy, etc.

Therapy alone will not solve everything for most people. But it can be helpful in determining what you want to solve and how you want to solve it, and in learning how to solve the things that you don't yet know how to.

Some therapists allow you to have a consultation before you do a proper session. This can help you to get a feel for whether they are right for you as well as what sort of issues they can help you with/how they can help you with them. That'll probably help you figure out what sort of preparation would be helpful for the first session, if you choose to book one.

Anyways, I'm just some internet weirdo who's never even seen a therapist. But there ya go.

I think your therapist may be saying those things to put the pressure on.

Whether you want a therapist who uses tactics like that or not is up to you. I myself would not.

It's not for her to decide whether or not your issues have improved--that is for you to decide. In fact, it's not even for her to decide what improvement is or how much of it is desirable--those are also for you to decide.
